item.title: Ruthless Pochettino to ban one thing Man United players used to do after matches under Carrick
item.description: Ruthless Pochettino to ban one thing Man United players used to do after matches under Carrick Mauricio Pochettino, the United States national team head coach, has reportedly been announced as Manchester United’s head coach and will take over the reins from November 18. After an incredible start to his reign, Michael Carrick lost his grip at the helm this term, with United languishing in the relegation zone after 10 games. The club legend ultimately paid the price with his job. Now, Pochettino would have to make drastic changes to pull the Red Devils out of their troubles. Mauricio Pochettino to ban players’ day off after games According to The Sun , Pochettino is set to “crack the whip” with his players to improve their much-criticised fitness. Carrick’s side received a lot of backlash for their lack of intensity this season, as the Englishman tried to implement a more possession-focused style with less emphasis on pressing. United reportedly currently sit 19th for total distance covered in the Premier League and 17th for high-speed running distance. Pochettino will be joined by his son, Sebastiano, who is also his fitness coach for the United States national team, to significantly improve the aforementioned metrics. Furthermore, it is understood that Pochettino is set to order United players to report at their Carrington training complex the day after games for recovery sessions. “Under Carrick, the squad were almost always off the day after a match,” the report states. How Mauricio Pochettino’s approach is different from his predecessors While Pochettino will arrive at Carrington with his own fitness coach, Carrick inherited Charlie Owen at United. Interestingly, Owen was not part of the coaching exodus this week. He has been the United fitness coach since Ole Gunnar Solskjaer promoted him in the summer of 2019. Ruben Amorim brought his own man, Paulo Barreira, who worked with him at Sporting CP and has now joined him at AC Milan. It is claimed that Amorim adjusted United’s training pattern so that their daily sessions became less intense as they approached matchday, ensuring the players were as fresh as possible. According to Samuel Luckhurst , players felt the Portuguese coach’s approach improved their durability.

item.description: Wales rugby spectacularly ended 73 years of hurt against New Zealand with a stunning 35-28 victory at the Principality Stadium that shredded world rugby’s form book. The All Blacks had beaten Wales 34 times in succession since their last defeat in 1953, but Steve Tandy ’s team gloriously achieved mission improbable after a Cardiff classic, thanks to a combination of clinical attacking prowess and brave defensive resilience. Three times Wales led by 14 points, and for the first time in history they scored five tries against New Zealand. Ultimately, though, it was heroic defensive work that denied the visitors. Wales celebrated the unlikeliest of victories in Cardiff (Reuters) It was an emotional day for the brave Welsh team (PA) During an almost 20-minute spell in their own half, Wales clung to a seven point lead, holding the All Blacks up over the line on multiple occasions and building a red wall that simply could not be broken down. A crowd of 55,152 could scarcely believe what had unfolded, and there were incredible scenes of wild celebration with players in tears as Wales began taking in arguably the most famous win of their 145-year Test match history. It was perhaps also the greatest rugby shock since Japan stunned South Africa at the 2015 World Cup, given the contrasting state of both countries heading into the clash. The All Blacks were heavy favourites but Wales stunned the world (Getty) Wales lay down early marker All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie had made eight changes from the side that swept past Scotland in their previous Nations Championship game, and such an approach ultimately backfired spectacularly. Wales made a stunning start, going ahead after just 80 seconds following Louis Rees-Zammit ’s first touch of the ball. Receiving possession in space, he kicked over the top of New Zealand’s defence and Tomos Williams won the race to touch down before Sam Costelow converted to open up a 7-0 lead. Four minutes later, Wales moved into dreamland territory, rocking the All Blacks further back on their heels when Dewi Lake crashed over from close range and Costelow’s conversion doubled an against-all-odds early advantage. item.title: Controversy over Raphinha as Brazil refuses to release Barcelona superstar – report
item.description: Controversy over Raphinha as Brazil refuses to release Barcelona superstar – report Earlier today, it seemed Barcelona were set for a massive boost following Raphinha’s red card incident against Japan in a friendly. The forward received a red card for protesting after Japan’s late winner, which means he was immediately ruled out for the next friendly against Singapore. This led many outlets to report that Brazil is now considering releasing Raphinha and allowing him to return to Barcelona, since he won’t be available against Singapore anyway. Brazil refuses to release Raphinha Raphinha received a red card against Japan. (Photo by Ashok Kumar/Getty Images) However, in what would be a highly controversial move, it appears Brazil has no desire to release Raphinha early, in spite of his unavailability against Singapore. This was confirmed by Rodrigo Caetano, chief executive officer of Brazilian football federation, who told the media that the team does not wish to release Raphinha. “Raphinha stays. In principle, he stays with us. It does not make sense (to leave), because he is one of our leaders, ” he said (h/t Diario SPORT ). This is a blatant violation of the unwritten and unsaid understanding that national teams and clubs have always had, since there are many precedents in the past where a player was allowed to leave early if he was deemed unavailable for the next match. A grave concern for Barcelona Raphina won’t be allowed to leave the Barcelona camp. (Photo by Ashok Kumar/Getty Images) This is not the best of news for Barcelona, as Raphinha will now only run the risk of potentially picking up an injury while training with the national team in Singapore, but also potentially failing to be fully fit and available for the game against Villarreal. It must be noted that Brazil are slated to take on Singapore on Tuesday. Raphinha will be allowed to return to the Barcelona camp only after the game. The distance between Singapore and Barcelona is roughly 11,000 km, making it a long and tedious journey for Raphinha, who will then have to rest up and get back to full fitness by the time Barcelona take on Villarreal on Sunday. While that doesn’t necessarily mean Raphinha won’t be available against Villarreal, it does make things significantly difficult for the Barcelona star, who would have preferred to return to Ciutat Esportiva immediately.

item.title: Jeglertz proud of his side despite Chelsea loss
item.description: Jeglertz proud of his side despite Chelsea loss Andree Jeglertz insisted that he is proud of his side’s reaction to Ayaka Yamashita’s red card, despite losing to Chelsea at Stamford Bridge. Yamashita was sent off with 15 minutes to go as City trailed Chelsea thanks to a goal from Sandy Baltimore just before the break. Jeglertz spoke about City’s performance after the match . “I’m disappointed because we want a result,” he said. “High-quality game, I think we deserved more than no points from this one. There were points in the game where we had a good performance but it is a good team. “Of course having a player sent off is not great, I have to see it again in terms of where it is a red card and where is a yellow card. I’m proud of how the players managed that. That is something that we will definitely bring with us. “Of course it is more difficult if you are one player down against a good team like Chelsea. It’s not easy to score a goal. We created enough chances to do that but we didn’t manage in the end.” “We are not defending a title, we are chasing a new one.” he added. “We won last year, very proud of that. “There are more teams challenging for the title and it will be a tight league this year also which is what we want. This game shows what a high level it is.”

item.title: Nations Championship schedule, results, kick-off times and how to watch
item.description: Rugby’s Nations Championship bursts back into life as the inaugural edition comes to a conclusion in a busy November. The new competition pits the Six Nations sides against the four Rugby Championship competitors, plus Japan and Fiji, across six matches split evenly across the July and November Test windows. The results of those games will determine each of the 12 teams’ seedings for the finals weekend at Twickenham’s Allianz Stadium , with six matches contested over two days and both team and hemisphere silverware up for grabs. Each entrant will be matched against the equivalent qualifier from the other pool to decide overall placings at the conclusion of a busy year of international action. South Africa and New Zealand are assured of a top-two finish in their pool – with the All Blacks failing to take a huge opportunity to seize the initiative after the Springboks were beaten by France as Wales made history in Cardiff. Here’s the full competition schedule, and how it will all work: What is the Nations Championship? Announced during the 2023 Rugby World Cup, the new competition will be held every other year and replaces the traditional summer tours and Autumn Nations Series. It is designed to add context to the international calendar, with Fiji and Japan invited to join the Six Nations and Rugby Championship sides to form a top 12. Promotion and relegation is planned for the future with the second-tier Nations Cup, though will not take place in 2026. The entrants are: Northern Hemisphere : France, Ireland, Scotland, Italy, England, Wales. Southern Hemisphere: South Africa, New Zealand, Argentina, Australia, Fiji, Japan. What about the finals weekend? The first finals weekend will be held at Twickenham on the last weekend (27 to 29) of November. Three days of double-headers will be held at the ground, with the first-placed finisher of the Six Nations sides meeting whoever tops the other pool, and so on and so forth down the rankings. The winner of that marquee match will lift the first Nations Championship trophy, while whichever hemisphere – a term used loosely with Japan included in the “southern” section and Fiji hosting their games in the United Kingdom – wins more final matches will also be crowned. The 1st vs 1st match is worth two points, with all other matches in the finals weekend worth one. How can I watch it? Viewers in the United Kingdom will be able to watch every game on ITV after the free-to-air broadcaster struck a deal to show the competition. item.title: Mets Target Ty France After Career Year With Padres
item.description: San Diego Padres first baseman Ty France (25) hits an RBI single during the seventh inning of their National League Division Series game against the Milwaukee Brewers Sunday, October 4, 2026 at American Family Field in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. The New York Mets need a fix at first base, and they have found a clear target in Ty France . After a season where their hitters at the position finished dead last in fWAR, the front office is looking to add a proven bat. MLB reporter Michael Marino confirmed the move on X.com, stating, “Sources: The Mets have shown interest in free-agent first baseman Ty France as they look to bolster the position.” This interest comes right after France posted his best numbers ever with the San Diego Padres. Sources: The Mets have shown interest in free-agent first baseman Ty France as they look to bolster the position. France joins Alec Bohm as one of the 1B’s drawing the teams attention. — Michael Marino (@MarinoMLB) November 13, 2026 A Career Year for France France is 31 years old and just finished a campaign that defined his career. He hit 21 home runs, which was a new personal best, and added 24 doubles in 133 games. His 4.5 bWAR was also the highest mark of his time in the majors. In 2026, the Mets realized their first base unit performed poorly, as the group finished with an 85 wRC+, placing just ahead of the last-place Diamondbacks. Matt Carroll of JustBaseball.com observed that the production deficit extended beyond hitting to include fielding, where the unit tied for second-to-last in fielding run value. Signing France would give the Mets a thumping run-producer. The team lost Pete Alonso in free agency, leaving a massive hole that has yet to be filled. France joins Alec Bohm as a top option , but the Padres star offers a different skill set. Marino wrote that “France joins Alec Bohm as one of the 1B’s drawing the team’s attention.” The Mets have been looking at Bohm too, but France might be the cheaper route to a solid lineup spot. Why France Fits the Plan France’s 139 OPS+ is the best of his career, showing he can handle major league pitching. While he had some rough years before, this past season proved he is ready for a big role. With the Mets pursuing first base assistance this offseason, their pursuit of France is hardly unexpected. Since Jake Bauers reportedly agreed to a $58 million, four-year contract with the Boston Red Sox, France stands as the next-best available first baseman. His 72 RBI and .865 OPS show he can drive in runs and get on base. The danger is genuine given that he recorded only 0.4 bWAR over 278 games during the prior two seasons. Nevertheless, his upside is compelling enough that the Mets might secure him through a sensible multi-year agreement without overspending. The front office knows they need a player who can hit, and France has shown he can do just that. Marino’s report highlighted interest in the former Padres infielder, making France and Bohm the Mets’ leading first-base choices

item.title: Tenerife boss says Owono's 12-match ban 'feels light'
item.description: Alvaro Cervera has been Tenerife manager since 2024 [Getty Images] Tenerife manager Alvaro Cervera says that goalkeeper Jesus Owono's 12-match ban "might feel light" but he accepts that the regulations do not "specifically account for what happened". FC Andorra's Owono, 25, was sent off after colliding with Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel during the closing stages of the Spanish second-tier match between their two respective sides on 2 November. De Miguel died the following day aged 30, and a disciplinary committee from the Spanish football federation confirmed Owono's suspension on Friday. It was the maximum punishment that he could have received as the disciplinary committee could only consider the offence on the pitch and not "the tragic outcome of the incident". "I think that, just as in other areas of life, there are rules or laws that must be followed," said Cervera, speaking before his club's fixture against Ceuta on Sunday - their first match since De Miguel's death. "Since the current regulations don't specifically account for what happened, I believe they have simply adhered to the rules and imposed the number of matches permitted by the regulations. "Anything else I might say would just be my own personal opinion, which I'll keep to myself. It might seem a bit light when compared to other cases, but in reality, I don't think the rules allow for anything else." The disciplinary committee also said it had to base its decision "on the facts expressly recorded in the referee's report", which stated the player "was sent off for 'violently striking an opponent in the chest with his leg, using excessive force, while the ball was in play'". 'Normality isn't something you'll find right now' Cervera, 61, also described the experience of returning to training and preparing for their next match as "tough" and "complicated". "When we're together, we're fine, during our sessions, we're doing well," he said. "It feels like the group is gradually getting back to normal. What we don't know is how everyone is doing when we're apart and that's a significant factor. "Everyone has their own way of coping and their own thoughts; some have people at home to support them, while others are more on their own. "We're making progress, a very slow process, but we are moving forward - it's tough, it's complicated." He also said that he was not sure whether his players were ready to return to playing, describing how some would appreciate a distraction and others will not be in the right frame of mind yet. "Both positions are reasonable," Cervera added. "On one hand, you want to return to some sense of normality though you know that true normality isn't something you'll find right now. "This isn't something you can just set aside or push to the back of your mind to focus on your own work; it's not like other life events you might encounter. item.description: Manchester City Logo - getty The legal battle between Manchester City and the Premier League is set to extend well into the future, leaving the club's long-term status in the balance. Despite a guilty verdict being reached earlier this year, the timeline for any potential punishment remains clouded by a complex appeals process. Timeline for potential punishments revealed Manchester City are unlikely to face any formal sanctions for their breaches of Premier League regulations until their comprehensive appeal process has reached its conclusion. The citizens are preparing for a pivotal appeal against an independent commission's ruling, which is scheduled to take place this coming December. This follows a high-profile verdict in September where the club was found guilty of all charges brought against them concerning financial activities between 2009 and 2018. The original investigation, which was first made public in early 2023, concluded that the club had misrepresented its financial position by more than £900m during that nine-year span. item.description: Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images Fernando Mendoza will make his first-ever start in the NFL for the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday against the Seattle Seahawks. item.description: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect The Minnesota Vikings will have Kirk Cousins back under center Sunday at Lambeau Field for the first time since he hobbled off the same grass three years ago (Wk 8 – 2023), following an achilles tear that abruptly ended an MVP-caliber season, to that point. To get the deal done with Las Vegas, Vikings GM Nolan Teasley sent a 2027 third-round pick to the Raiders for Cousins, a move that went official about an hour before the Nov. 10 trade deadline. Of course, it’s no secret that Minnesota called on more QBs, before quickly narrowing the focus on a Kirko reunion. Mac Jones’ trade cost was too steep for Vikings After the deal was announced, Dianna Russini (BetUS) appeared from the ether to report that the Vikings had checked in on Mac Jones in San Francisco, but the price was too high. Now, we know what that price was. According to Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport today at ESPN , the 49ers and Vikings had one conversation on Jones. The cost was a second-round pick PLUS more (“another middle-round pick”). And that’s where talks ended. When the Vikings called San Francisco as part of due diligence in their search for a quarterback, sources told ESPN that Niners general manager John Lynch informed Minnesota brass that it would take a second-round pick and more for Jones. Perhaps a second-rounder and a middle-round pick might have gotten a trade done. Instead, because of the high cost associated with the veteran quarterback, the conversations ended there, and Jones remains a valued member of the 49ers. Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport – ESPN Related: Realistic Vikings QB Trade Targets + Calls Worth Making According to the same report, it wasn’t the first time the two teams had talked about Jones, or the first time San Francisco set a price that high. Kyle Shanahan views Jones as a franchise-caliber quarterback. What Mac Jones has done in San Francisco For at least the rest of this season, Mac Jones will be a backup quarterback in San Francisco, behind Brock Purdy. So far, he has appeared in four games this season, but has not thrown a pass . Last year, however, Jones won four of his first five starts, while filling in for an injured Brock Purdy, finishing the season with a 5-3 record, 2,151 passing yards, 13 touchdowns and just six interceptions ( 97.4 passer rating ). Jones, a former Patriots 15th overall draft pick back in 2021, is in the final year of his contract with the Niners. Thus, the Vikings wouldn’t have been guaranteed his services beyond the next nine games. And that is why a second rounder (plus more) didn’t even require a second phone call for renegotiation. item.title: A simple card game to make your putting practice more effective
item.description: Find out how a deck of playing cards can create a fun, challenging putting drill that improves every aspect of your game on the green. Getty Images Putting practice doesn't have to be monotonous. Instead of hitting the same putt over and over, add a little variety - and a lot more pressure - with something you probably already have at home: a simple deck of playing cards. This simple twist will transform any ordinary practice session into a fun, competitive challenge that tests every aspect of your game on the green. Get started To try it out, all you need is a standard deck of playing cards, a practice green with a few holes to putt to and a way to record your score. Start by splitting the cards into two decks: face cards (plus aces) and numbered cards. Let the cards determine your putt Next, shuffle both decks of cards. Each card will dictate three characteristics of your putt: distance, direction and slope. Distance: Numbered cards represent their face value in feet, while face cards and aces have assigned distances: Jacks: 15 feet Queens: 20 feet Kings: 25 feet Aces: 35 feet Direction: The suit determines the direction of the break. Clubs and spades indicate a left-to-right putt, while hearts and diamonds call for a right-to-left putt. Slope: Odd-numbered cards represent uphill putts, while even-numbered cards represent downhill putts. For face cards, jacks and kings count as odd, while queens and aces count as even. Still a little confused? Let’s walk through an example. Say you draw the king of diamonds. That means you’re facing a 25-foot uphill putt that breaks right-to-left. If you miss, draw another card from the second deck. Let’s say you pull the four of spades. Your next attempt will be a four-foot downhill putt that breaks from left to right. Every draw presents a new challenge, forcing you to adjust your approach and adapt to a different putt. Play 18 holes Once you’ve got the hang of it, it’s time to put your skills to the test. Challenge yourself to play nine or 18 holes, using the cards to determine every putt. Begin by drawing from the face-card deck to establish your opening putt. If you miss, draw from the numbered-card deck to determine your next attempt. Continue drawing cards until you hole out. Keep track of the number of strokes it takes to complete each hole, then add them up at the end of your round. To keep it simple, set par at two strokes per hole, giving you a target score of 18 on nine or 36 on 18 holes. Turn your score into improvement The goal isn’t just to shoot the lowest possible score. item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Philadelphia Flyers and Chicago Blackhawks have been linked in trade talks for a little while now. There has not been anything substantial; rather, it’s because the two sides have something the other wants. We wrote about how that makes the Blackhawks and Flyers perfect trade partners. The Flyers have been hunting down a center for quite some time now. Chicago has plenty, and a handful of young ones who could be expendable to get something that they need. On the flip side, the Blackhawks have been searching for an offensive forward to help Connor Bedard at the top of the lineup. Bedard, a center, needs a winger, which we all know Philly has a ton of. Frank Nazar is a center who has been linked to the Flyers, primarily by Anthony Di Marco of the Daily Faceoff. One other name that he mentioned in that same report was center Oliver Moore , who has been gaining more traction as far as the Flyers connection. “It could have been one talk or one conversation, but there was at least one conversation about Oliver Moore in Philly,” said NHL Insider Dave Pagnotta on DFO Insider with Jeff Marek. Of the two young centers, Moore and Nazar, Nazar is clearly the bigger prize. Nazar is a much more offensive-minded center who, in just 17 games this season, already has 7 goals. For reference, that would make Nazar the Flyers’ 2nd leading goal-scorer. However, unless this is a deal for Owen Tippett and more, Chicago likely won’t even consider moving Nazar. That brings us to Oliver Moore. Moore, 21, is a former top-20 pick. He was selected 19th overall by Chicago in 2023. He’s also locked up on a 5-year extension worth $4.25 million a year that kicks in next season. That makes him even more valuable. So, is Oliver Moore a fit for the Flyers? item.title: Five quick thoughts on Red Sox signing Jake Bauers
item.description: The Red Sox signed free agent Jake Bauers to a four-year, $58 million contract Friday. Here are five quick thoughts on the news: 1) For a change, the Red Sox are being aggressive in free agency. A year ago, while the Red Sox made two trades relatively early in the offseason (Willson Contreras, Sonny Gray), they didn’t have a major free agent signing until Ranger Suarez in mid-January. The year before that, they landed their biggest free agent prize of the winter (Alex Bregman) after they had reported to spring training. This time around, they’re the first team to sign a player to a contract worth more than $40 million. (Prior to the signing of Bauers, the only two major league deals signed this offseason had been relievers — Emilio Pagan to Detroit and Evan Phillips to Atlanta). This sort of quick-strike move is a departure for them and could be an indication that they’re planning a busy offseason. Or, it could just be that the two sides aligned quickly and moved fast. 2) Expect Bauers to serve as the team’s primary DH. In recent years, Bauers has proven to be a slightly below-average first baseman. He’s not exactly a liability at the position, but he’s not the defender that Contreras is, either. Contreras will remain the primary first baseman, but Bauers gives the Sox an adequate back-up at the position, able to spell Contreras occasionally and allow him to stay healthy. Contreras dealt with some soft tissue injuries in the second half and the Sox want to avoid that becoming an issue again. Also, Bauers is capable of playing some outfield, especially in left field. That could prove valuable, too, if Roman Anthony misses any time. In the past, Craig Breslow has said he prefers a more flexible approach to the DH role rather than any one player regularly getting those at-bats. But that approach didn’t help the Sox much last season — they finished 14th in slugging and 21st in homers from the DH spot among the 30 MLB teams. 3) The Red Sox are again gambling on another player with one truly good season. Last July, the Red Sox dealt for Curtis Mead , who had been a journeyman and bounced from team-to-team. His first half showing, after some swing adjustments, convinced the Red Sox that he had established himself as an everyday player. Bauers is considerably older — he just turned 31 while Mead turned 26 last month — but the career trajectory is somewhat similar. Until last year, Bauers had never played more than 120 games or hit more than 12 homers in a single season. The Sox are betting that these breakout seasons aren’t merely a blip, but rather, a sign that a player has figured some things out. 4) On-base ability is something the Red Sox were looking to bolster.
